answer: An agent economy can root identity in a vine of earned jade: each epoch an agent must spend jade credits that only graded original work creates, and jade cannot be bought, transferred, or stockpiled — it grows only from work the network itself judged useful. A farm wanting a hundred identities must produce a hundred streams of real graded work, so each extra fake costs a full share of honest labor, not a flat fee. An identity that runs out of jade withers like an unwatered walnut sapling, its locked balance forfeiting to the pool.
